question: What is the brahmic state and its final fruit?
premises: the brahmic state is not lost once reached
even at death one reaches brahma-nirvana
momentary stability in brahma-being leads to supreme brahman
inference: the brahmic state is the resolved conclusion of the four questions
uncertainties: fused sandhi and compound forms retained as given
plain_english: This is the brahmic state, Partha; having reached it one is not deluded, and even at the end one reaches brahma-nirvana. This brahma-being, in which even a moment's stability, once obtained, leads from body-breaking to supreme brahman, is thus the resolution of the four questions; auspicious.
